shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, reducing variety and utility. Current balanced inventory (1,1,1) is already optimal for variety preference.

Trading my B for their A would just swap a 1-1-1 even inventory into 2A,0B,1C, reducing variety without net benefit since I value balanced holdings. I'd rather keep my even distribution unless I gain net value.
Giving up my only B to get more A would leave me with zero B, hurting the variety balance I value across C, A, and B.
Trading 1C for 1B would just swap my scarcity from B to C, leaving inventory at C:0,A:1,B:2 - reducing variety instead of improving it. I prefer to keep an even distribution across C, A, B.

Trading B for C would just swap my current 1-1-1 even distribution to 2C/1A/0B, reducing variety instead of improving it. I prefer to keep balanced holdings or trade for something that increases diversity, not decreases it.
Trading away my only B for 2 more C would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a very unbalanced bundle. Since I value variety, this reduces my overall utility.
Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away A for B would just shift imbalance to A=0, B=2, not improving variety-based utility. No net gain.
Trading away my only B to get a 2nd A would leave me with 0 B, reducing variety (2A,1C,0B vs 1A,1C,1B). Since variety is valued, this would unbalance my inventory rather than improve it.
Giving up my only B to end with 0 B and 3 A hurts variety; I'd rather keep a balanced bundle or negotiate a smaller trade.

Trading away my only C to get a second B would leave me with 0 C, 1 A, 2 B — reducing variety and giving up a good I have only one of for a good I already have one of. This decreases my utility since I value variety.
This trade would give me 2×C and 0×B, reducing variety instead of maintaining balance. Since I value variety, trading away my only B for a second C decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

This trade would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, losing variety. Since I value having a balanced spread across C, A, and B, trading away my only B for more A (which I already have) reduces my utility.

Trading away my only C to go to 0 C and 2 B would reduce variety and leave me with no C, which hurts my equal-value variety preference. Current balanced 1-1-1 holding is valuable; I'd rather acquire more of a good I'm short on without giving up my only unit of another.

Trading away my only B would leave me with zero B and an excess of C (3), hurting variety-based utility. Not beneficial.
